messages:
Jordan: FYI privacy portal received a 'right to suppress' DSAR for user@example.com (EU). No legal hold flagged but curious about old nightly snapshots and our deep cold backups. Also we rotated the primary KMS key last month in us-east1  does that break decrypt for older snapshots? :thinking:
Tessa: Quick checks  1) request origin automated or manual? 2) any ongoing litigation flag?
Jordan: Generated via privacy webhook (verif id 8923). Manual review queued. No litigation tag.
Mohit: If no hold, plan: scrub live vectors + metadata + update provenance. KMS rotation matters if backups reference old key and we lack a rewrap path. Need inventory of snapshots that reference key-2023-rotated. Also avoid permanent broad RBAC grants for erasure jobs  prefer ephemeral scoped role.
Oliver: Agree. We'll provision an ephemeral service principal eraser-runner with least privilege: list/read/delete on vector-store objects, delete/mark on snapshot manifests, and write-audit permission. Infra can either grant short-lived creds or run the scrub in infra account.
audit-bot: Scan results: found 2 vector indices and 2 S3 snapshots where email=user@example.com. Snapshots: snap-20240118, snap-20240201. Encryption metadata: snap-20240118 -> key-2019, snap-20240201 -> key-2023-rotated.
Tessa: So snap-20240201 likely decryptable if infra retained previous key material. Mohit, can you check KMS logs whether key-2023-rotated was a rotate-with-preserve or rotate-with-destroy?
Mohit: Checking KMS now. Confirmed rotate-with-preserve; we retained old key version and documented rewrap metadata. Infra keeps a keystore backup for 90 days. Decryption for scrub feasible but coordinate with infra.
Jordan: Proposed runbook:
1) Confirm no legal hold (done).
2) Create ephemeral RBAC role data-erasure:grant for eraser-runner (TTL 4h).
3) Dry-run: run erase dry-run that enumerates targets and emits planned-audit entries (no deletes).
4) Infra decrypt step: ask infra to temporarily allow rewrap/decrypt for snapshots referencing key-2023-rotated. Send ticket with snapshots list.
5) Execute: run scrub job to delete vectors, scrub metadata, and write immutable audit entries and deletion receipt to privacy portal.
6) Backups: if offline cold backups contain data post-run, file a retention-exception and provide timeline + mitigation to requester.

Tessa: I'll create the ephemeral RBAC grant and schedule the dry-run. Oliver, can infra respond to decrypt ticket once I open it?
Oliver: Yes. Email kms-access@infra with ticket id + snapshot list. We may need a short maintenance window for archived snapshot rewraps.
Mohit: Dry-run commands/examples:
```
-- find vectors by email
SELECT id, index_name FROM vectors WHERE metadata->>'email' = 'user@example.com';

# dry-run call to internal erase endpoint
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ERASER_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://api.redwood.internal/v1/erase -d '{"email":"user@example.com","dry_run":true}'
```
Jordan: I'll verify dry-run output and sign-off for the real run. If infra cannot decrypt any snapshot within 24h, I'll open a retention-exception with privacy and legal and notify the requester timeline.
Tessa: Add audit assertions: every deletion must emit immutable audit entry including actor, scope, preimage-hash, request_id, and job-id. Also retain dry-run logs in case legal requests proof of attempted erasure.
Oliver: Note: some cold archives are immutable object stores with long retention. If infra confirms any such archive contains records, we'll need a formal retention-exception and comms plan to the data subject. Documenting exception and expected purge timeline is critical.
Jordan: I'll update the privacy ticket with the runbook and attach dry-run logs when available. Thanks all :thumbsup:
